title: Passage from complete scalar tests to norm-topological algebraic-closure scalar tests
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its norm topology [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], and an algebraic closure $\Omega\supset E$ with its extended norm topology. Let $I$ be a small directed poset with least element $0$, and let $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system of regular affine finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume every transition $X_j\to X_i$ is finite locally free, meaning affine with locally finite free coordinate module [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Choose $f_0\in\Gamma(X_0,\mathcal O_{X_0})$ whose pullback $f_i$ is a nonzerodivisor for every $i$, and put $X=\operatorname{Spec}(\varinjlim_i\Gamma(X_i,\mathcal O_{X_i}))$ and $W=X[1/f_0]$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For a normed field $F$ put $C_F(P)=C(P,F)$ on profinite sets using all continuous maps, and $C_{F,Z}=p_Z^*C_F$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use ordinary derived categories of abelian sheaves and K-injective derived sections [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology].

Assume that for every affine weakly contractible pro-etale $v:V\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, sk-def-pe-weak-contractible], with $T=V\times_XW$, restriction on the constant sheaf $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$ induces a bijection on degree-zero sections [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Assume also that, for every such $V,T$ and every complete nonarchimedean normed field $B$ extending $\mathbf Q_\ell$ isometrically, the actual restriction $R\Gamma(V,C_{B,V}[0])\to R\Gamma(T,C_{B,T}[0])$ is an isomorphism.

Then for every such $V,T$ and $F=E,\Omega$, the actual scalar restriction
$$R\Gamma(V,C_{F,V}[0])\longrightarrow R\Gamma(T,C_{F,T}[0])$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$. In degree zero it is restriction of all continuous $F$-valued functions. In positive degrees $H^q(T,C_{F,T})=0$. No completeness of $\Omega$ and no replacement of $C(-,\Omega)$ by a union of finite-extension-valued function sheaves is assumed. Empty test schemes and identity opens are allowed.

proof.text: Fix a test $V$ and put $T=V[1/f_V]$. The finite constant representation identifies sections of $\mathbf Z/\ell$ on either scheme with locally constant functions to the finite discrete field. A morphism to the labelled coproduct is precisely its clopen partition into label fibres. Naturality in finite label maps identifies multiplication and constants pointwise. Hence the hypothesized restriction bijection is a ring isomorphism. Its idempotents are characteristic functions of clopens: pointwise $a^2=a$ implies $a=0$ or $1$, and conversely each such characteristic function is locally constant. Restriction and its inverse preserve idempotents, so inverse image $\operatorname{Clop}(V)\to\operatorname{Clop}(T)$ is bijective.

source.place: Tag 0H7J, example-constant-sheaf; finite labelled-coproduct realization, followed by the elementary idempotent calculation.

proof.text: The schemes $V$ and $T$ are affine, the latter being a principal open of the former. Thus both are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], and spectral by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral]. Apply [lem-sfb-spectral-clopen-component-homeomorphism] to the continuous inclusion $j:T\to V$ and step 1. It gives a homeomorphism $h:\pi_0(T)\to\pi_0(V)$, with $h q_T=q_Vj$, where $q$ denotes the quotient map to connected components.

source.place: Tag 0906, lemma-spectral-pi0, through the existing clopen component-homeomorphism criterion; properties.tex Tag 094L, lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-spectral.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value], $E$ is nonarchimedean. Any two elements of $\Omega$ lie in a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, so the same lemma makes its given extended norm nonarchimedean. Both fields are totally disconnected: for $a\ne b$, the ball $|x-a|<|a-b|$ contains $a$, excludes $b$, and is clopen. Indeed any point outside this ball has a ball disjoint from it by the ultrametric inequality. A connected subset therefore cannot contain two distinct points. The continuous-function realization now identifies $\Gamma(Z,C_{F,Z})$ with $C(|Z|,F)$ for $Z=V,T$ and $F=E,\Omega$. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] the open $T$ is an object of $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is the slice at it; the realization on $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is an isomorphism of sheaves, so it commutes with restriction to $T$, which therefore becomes precomposition by $j$.

source.place: Example 3.1, continuous-function realization; ultrametric separation written out using the existing finite-extension absolute-value theorem.

proof.text: Every continuous $g:|T|\to F$ is constant on each connected component, since its image on that component is connected and $F$ is totally disconnected. Its induced function $\bar g:\pi_0(T)\to F$ is continuous by the definition of quotient topology. Its unique extension to $V$ is $\bar g h^{-1}q_V$; restricting gives $g$, because $h q_T=q_Vj$. Conversely every continuous function on $V$ factors through $q_V$, so the surjectivity of $h$ proves uniqueness. Step 3 identifies this inverse with the inverse to the actual degree-zero coefficient restriction. This works also for empty spaces.

source.place: Elementary quotient-topology factorization and composition with the component homeomorphism from step 2.

proof.text: Evaluation on an affine weakly contractible $V$ preserves homology by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-abelian-evaluation-colimits]. Applied to a K-injective resolution $C_{F,V}[0]\to J$, it shows that $C_{F,V}(V)[0]\to J(V)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus $H^q(V,C_{F,V})=0$ for $q>0$, for any of our coefficient fields. This is the same evaluation functor on the small site of $V$: by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is the slice $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/V$, whose final object is $V$; an epimorphism in the slice is an epimorphism over $h_V$ in $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and a lift over $V$ of a section lying over $\mathrm{id}_V$ still lies over $\mathrm{id}_V$, so $V$ is weakly contractible in $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ as well. For $F=E$, completeness [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-complete] and step 3 allow the assumed complete-field restriction test with $B=E$. It proves the required actual derived restriction for $E$ and $H^q(T,C_{E,T})=0$ for $q>0$.

proof.text: Form $\widehat\Omega$ by [lem-sfb-normed-field-completion]. Its canonical inclusion is isometric, so its restriction to $\mathbf Q_\ell$ is isometric. Its norm is nonarchimedean: approximate two completed elements by sequences in $\Omega$ and pass the ultrametric inequality to the limit, using continuity of norm, addition and maximum. The assumed complete-field test therefore applies to $B=\widehat\Omega$. Step 5 gives $H^q(V,C_{\widehat\Omega,V})=0$, whence $H^q(T,C_{\widehat\Omega,T})=0$ for $q\ge1$. Apply [lem-sfb-norm-completion-positive-cohomology-mono] to the given regular affine finite-type tower, its finite locally free transitions, the stagewise nonzerodivisors and our affine weakly contractible $V$. Its map into these zero groups is injective; thus $H^q(T,C_{\Omega,T})=0$ for every $q\ge1$.

proof.text: For either $Z=V,T$, sections on abelian sheaves are left exact: kernels and finite limits are computed sectionwise. Abelian sheaves are modules over the constant integer ring sheaf; [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] gives the Grothendieck hypothesis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing] with bound $0$ to obtain $H^q(R\Gamma(Z,C_{F,Z}[0]))=0$ for $q<0$. The bounded-below computation agrees with the stipulated unbounded K-injective computation by [src-right-derived-functor-plus-compatibility]. In degree zero, left exactness identifies the kernel of the first differential of a nonnegative injective resolution with the original sections, naturally for restriction. Consequently the actual restriction for $\Omega$ induces the bijection of step 4 in degree zero and maps between zero groups in all other degrees by steps 5--6. On resolution complexes this is a quasi-isomorphism, hence is inverted in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This proves all claims, including the identity open and empty cases.
